reason: Eight concrete GA4 Data API reporting tools registered unconditionally with FastMCP; source and Docker entrypoints invoke this server.

tools.name: google_analytics_get_overview
tools.description:
Returns the main KPIs of the GA4 property for the selected period.

Metrics: sessions, active users, new users, pageviews, bounce rate,
average session duration, engagement rate and conversions.
With compare_previous=True, includes a percentage comparison against
the previous period.

Args:
    params (OverviewInput): property_id, period, compare_previous, format.

Returns:
    str: KPIs as markdown (default) or structured JSON.

property_id.title: Property Id
property_id.description: Numeric GA4 property ID (e.g. 123456789). If omitted, uses GOOGLE_ANALYTICS_PROPERTY_ID from the environment.

date_range.title: Date Range
date_range.description: Period: last_7_days (default), last_14_days, last_30_days, this_month, last_month or custom.

start_date.title: Start Date
start_date.description: Start date for date_range='custom'. Format: YYYY-MM-DD.

end_date.title: End Date
end_date.description: End date for date_range='custom'. Format: YYYY-MM-DD.

compare_previous.title: Compare Previous
compare_previous.description: If True, includes a comparison against the previous same-sized period.

response_format.title: Response Format
response_format.description: 'markdown' for human reading (default) or 'json' for structured data.

tools.behavior: Calls runReport for sessions, activeUsers, newUsers, screenPageViews, bounceRate, averageSessionDuration, engagementRate and conversions. Optionally adds the immediately preceding equal-length date range and dateRange dimension; returns numeric current/previous metrics and periods. Markdown computes percentage deltas; JSON returns raw structured comparison data. Uses the per-call property_id or environment default, resolves presets when applicable, and returns formatted Markdown or JSON text. Configuration/API/timeouts/unexpected errors are caught and returned as strings.
notes: Input model strips surrounding whitespace from strings and rejects extra model fields.
date_range='custom' requires both dates at handler time; schema permits either to be null/omitted. Date strings have a shape regex, without calendar-validity or chronological-order validation.

tools.name: google_analytics_get_traffic_sources
tools.description:

Per-source metrics: sessions, users, new users, bounce rate,
engagement rate and conversions.

Args:

Returns:

property_id.title: Property Id
property_id.description: Numeric GA4 property ID. If omitted, uses GOOGLE_ANALYTICS_PROPERTY_ID.

tools.behavior: Calls runReport grouped by sessionDefaultChannelGroup, sessionSource/sessionMedium, or sessionDefaultChannelGroup/sessionCampaignName; reports sessions, activeUsers, newUsers, bounceRate, engagementRate and conversions, sorted descending by sessions with the requested limit. Uses the per-call property_id or environment default, resolves presets when applicable, and returns formatted Markdown or JSON text. Configuration/API/timeouts/unexpected errors are caught and returned as strings.
notes: Input model strips surrounding whitespace from strings and rejects extra model fields.
date_range='custom' requires both dates at handler time; schema permits either to be null/omitted. Date strings have a shape regex, without calendar-validity or chronological-order validation.

tools.name: google_analytics_get_top_pages
tools.description:

page_path_filter.title: Page Path Filter
page_path_filter.description: Filter pages whose path starts with this prefix (e.g. '/blog', '/products').

tools.behavior: Calls runReport grouped by pagePath and pageTitle for screenPageViews, sessions, activeUsers, averageSessionDuration, bounceRate and engagementRate; sorts descending by screenPageViews and optionally applies a pagePath BEGINS_WITH string filter. Uses the per-call property_id or environment default, resolves presets when applicable, and returns formatted Markdown or JSON text. Configuration/API/timeouts/unexpected errors are caught and returned as strings.
notes: Input model strips surrounding whitespace from strings and rejects extra model fields.

Markdown additionally highlights most conversions and most sessions with zero conversions among returned locations. Uses the per-call property_id or environment default, resolves presets when applicable, and returns formatted Markdown or JSON text. Configuration/API/timeouts/unexpected errors are caught and returned as strings.

tools.name: google_analytics_get_events
tools.description:
Lists the most-triggered events on the GA4 property.

Returns event name, total count, count per user and total users.
With event_names, filters to only the specified events.

Args:
    params (EventsInput): property_id, period, event_names (optional filter),
        limit and format.

Returns:
    str: Events ordered by count as markdown or JSON.

property_id.title: Property Id
property_id.description: Numeric GA4 property ID. If omitted, uses GOOGLE_ANALYTICS_PROPERTY_ID.

event_names.title: Event Names
event_names.description: Filter only these events (e.g. ['purchase', 'sign_up']). If None, returns all.

tools.behavior: Calls runReport grouped by eventName for eventCount, eventCountPerUser and totalUsers, sorted descending by eventCount. A nonempty event_names list adds an eventName inListFilter. Uses the per-call property_id or environment default, resolves presets when applicable, and returns formatted Markdown or JSON text. Configuration/API/timeouts/unexpected errors are caught and returned as strings.
notes: Input model strips surrounding whitespace from strings and rejects extra model fields.
date_range='custom' requires both dates at handler time; schema permits either to be null/omitted. Date strings have a shape regex, without calendar-validity or chronological-order validation.
An empty event_names list applies no filter.

tools.name: google_analytics_get_conversions
tools.description:
Returns conversion and revenue data by channel and conversion event.

Only events flagged as conversions in GA4 appear here.
Includes conversion and revenue totals.

Args:
    params (ConversionsInput): property_id, period, limit and format.

Returns:
    str: Conversions table with revenue as markdown or JSON.

property_id.title: Property Id
property_id.description: Numeric GA4 property ID. If omitted, uses GOOGLE_ANALYTICS_PROPERTY_ID.

tools.behavior: Calls runReport grouped by sessionDefaultChannelGroup and eventName for conversions, totalRevenue and sessions; filters conversions GREATER_THAN 0 and sorts descending by conversions. Returns rows and locally summed conversion/revenue totals. Uses the per-call property_id or environment default, resolves presets when applicable, and returns formatted Markdown or JSON text. Configuration/API/timeouts/unexpected errors are caught and returned as strings.
notes: Input model strips surrounding whitespace from strings and rejects extra model fields.
date_range='custom' requires both dates at handler time; schema permits either to be null/omitted. Date strings have a shape regex, without calendar-validity or chronological-order validation.
Totals are sums over returned limited rows, not independent property-wide aggregate totals.

tools.name: google_analytics_get_realtime
tools.description:
Returns realtime data on currently active users (last 30 minutes).

Shows total active users and breakdowns by page, source, country
and device. Does not accept a date_range — always reflects the current state.

Args:
    params (RealtimeInput): property_id and format.

Returns:
    str: Active users and breakdowns as markdown or JSON.

property_id.title: Property Id
property_id.description: Numeric GA4 property ID. If omitted, uses GOOGLE_ANALYTICS_PROPERTY_ID.

tools.behavior: Makes five sequential runRealtimeReport requests for activeUsers: total, unifiedPagePathScreen, firstUserSource, country and deviceCategory. Each breakdown is sorted descending by activeUsers and limited to 10 rows. Returns numeric total and breakdown lists. Uses the per-call property_id or environment default, resolves presets when applicable, and returns formatted Markdown or JSON text. Configuration/API/timeouts/unexpected errors are caught and returned as strings.
notes: Input model strips surrounding whitespace from strings and rejects extra model fields.

All five requests must succeed; a failure discards earlier data and returns the shared error string. The source forwards unifiedPagePathScreen and firstUserSource to the realtime API without compatibility checks.
Source review only, no tools/list or live requests. HEAD matches assigned revision.

All eight tools are unconditional; MCP_PUBLIC_URL selects OAuth-enabled FastMCP construction, not a different tool inventory. HTTP mode requires Google web OAuth credentials; stdio entrypoint requires refresh-token credentials. A property_id or GOOGLE_ANALYTICS_PROPERTY_ID is required at call time.
Schemas reconstructed from AST annotations and Pydantic Field declarations; nested required params object retained, enums expanded, no upstream code executed.

pyproject.toml wheel packages selects only src while console script points to main:main; standalone wheel installation may omit root main.py. Source execution and Docker invoke the existing main.py directly.

Async tool functions invoke synchronous httpx reporting calls. Shared client retries once after a 401 by clearing cached access token; in HTTP injected-token mode this leaves no refresh credentials, causing a configuration error on retry.

review.method: Independently compared eight Python signatures/docstrings and all 49 nested Pydantic model fields against Field defaults/descriptions/bounds/patterns/enums; inspected report client requests, realtime limits, formatters and source versus wheel entrypoints.
